summary: SDKs and CLI that give AI agents ready-authenticated tools for 1000+ apps such as email, calendars and GitHub, with per-user sessions.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Composio is the SDK monorepo for the Composio platform. It gives your agents 1000+ toolkits for real apps, handles each user's sign-in to those apps, and adds triggers and a sandbox. It includes a TypeScript SDK, a Python SDK, a CLI and adapters for agent frameworks.
sixtySeconds.problem: Connecting an agent to Gmail, Slack, GitHub and other apps means building OAuth flows and API wrappers for each one. Composio provides them ready to use.
whoFor: Developers building agents that act in real apps
Teams adding app integrations to an AI product
Coding-agent users who want a tool CLI
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it to skip writing per-app integrations and auth. A session finds, authenticates and runs tools at runtime, and can also be used as an MCP endpoint.
requirements: An agent framework such as OpenAI Agents

overview: You create a session for one of your users, give its tools to your agent and let the agent act across apps. By default a session exposes meta tools that discover, authenticate and execute app tools when needed, so you don't load hundreds of tool definitions.
Adapters cover the OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, Vercel AI SDK, LangChain and more. Each session can also expose a hosted MCP URL for Claude, Cursor or other MCP clients.
The composio CLI lets you search, run and script tools from the shell. The SDKs are MIT licensed; the platform itself is a hosted service.
